 Rumour: Days Gone Dev to Announce and Launch New PS5 Game in 2027 
 Third-person game with co-op, it's reported
 by Liam Croft 
 12am 
 Share:
 Bend Studio, the first-party team best known for Days Gone , plans to reveal and potentially even release its next game in 2027.
 That's according to a new MP1st report , which shares more details on the project. The outlet claims an announcement will take place next year and it's "much further along in development" than you might think, so much so that Bend Studio is also planning to release it in 2027.
 MP1st calls the project a third-person experience with co-op features, but it's not a live service title.
 The website also claims it won't be a sequel to Days Gone. Previous reports stated Bend Studio pitched a Days Gone 2 to Sony after the first game, but it was turned down. It then actually did turn its attention to a Game as a Service, though this was cancelled at the start of last year .
 Now, according to the outlet, Bend Studio is gearing up to announce and release its project next year. With Until Dawn 2 , God of War Laufey , and potentially also Intergalactic slated for 2027, it could be a busy 12 months for Sony's first-party developers.
 This is just the latest report from MP1st surrounding PlayStation's unannounced plans. It has also suggested a Killzone project is in the works, and teased what to expect from Media Molecule next.

 New horizons
 With a new PS5 title around the corner, Bend Studio is indeed best known for Days Gone, as its biggest and most recent project. However, the developer has been part of Sony for over 20 years. In that time, it also made tons of Syphon Filter games, Resistance: Retribution for PSP, and Uncharted: Golden Abyss on the PS Vita.
 With a Days Gone sequel ruled out, what do you hope Bend Studio is working on? Let us know in the comments below.
 [source mp1st.com ]

 Syphon Filter was once a hit but it eventually ran out of gas commercially (for my money the portable games were the best in the series but I didn’t get the sense they were the hits the PS1 games were) and the creators stated they wanted to move on.
 Of course wanting to move on but returning to a franchise or character when fans fail to move with them is a thing, but I while I like Gabe Logan and his taser I think rolling the dice on an original game would be the smarter move.
 https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2025/07/may-2025-usa-sales-ps5-the-only-console-with-growth-as-xbox-price-hike-proves-costly

I haven’t put much time into a From game since Demon’s Souls (I will tackle Elden Ring some day when I am feeling the need to get my teeth kicked in 😋) but commercially From hasn’t missed in a long while. Lots of SP studios decide ‘I can do multiplayer too’ but few succeed.
 I’m a little saddened but unsurprised by the fact Days Gone Remastered (in stark contrast to Oblivion which also hit at the tail end of April) doesn’t seem to have charted. Days Gone eventually shaped up to be a good game (the rough state in which it launched is pretty common now but was unusual at the time) but it had the bad luck to be released in the same timeframe as The Last of Us (a better game and one which launched in a finished state) and unfortunately for Days TLOU still looms large. Dealing with a massive horde of running zombies is great fun though so maybe like the original game the Days Gone Remaster will have decent legs.

 Let's review, shall we?
 The last game released in 2019. It was review bombed by biased reviewers hell-Bend on a culture war that has yet to culminate. People like me trusted them leading to poorer sales than if reviews had reflected the actual quality of the product and not the reviewers virtue-signalling.
 And then a group of people in Bend manage to ruin the momentum even further and along the way ousts the talent that had the vision for Days Gone 2.
 7 years later and no games, no dlc, no nothing. Bend releases a remaster of Days Gone which suddenly isn't a problem for them to work on. They've done ***** all but exploit the success of Days Gone which by the way has continued to astonish new players with its quality to this day
 All along the way, you've got these self-important devs saying next to nothing and asking for patience without anything to show for it.
 The only conclusion I can draw from this: They're only still in existence because of revenue garnered from Days Gone. They'll get shuttered soon.
 EDIT 
I like your instinct to say there's too much crying about this, and wanting to cancel that.
 But remember, Sony has finite resources and will shut down someone's favorite studio only to create and find something like Haven (or Bend in this case).
 Another example is EA axing Mass Effect to support Battlefront if the rumours speak true.
